title: Grateful Dead Live at Rose Palace on 1969-05-10
source: Cassette Master (Recorded By Bear on a Concord F-400 Cassette Deck) - Cassette (Ampex C-90) Playback Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck No Dolby - Panasonic SV-3700 DAT @ 44.1KHz (DL)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording marred by harsh mid‑set diginoise, yet the Dark Star segment delivers a rare burst of electrifying interplay.
ai_review.review: The show features an outstanding Dark Star that many reviewers describe as “splendid” and full of energy, with the organ providing vivid cues for Jerry’s improvisations. Unfortunately the soundboard source suffers from severe interference and metallic doubling beginning around the 14‑minute mark, making large portions of the performance nearly unlistenable. While the musical peaks shine through, the technical flaws dominate most listeners’ experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Performance highlights (especially Dark Star) are praised, but the majority of reviewers criticize the recording’s severe noise and tape degradation; the mixed feedback from six reviews yields a moderate overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Severe diginoise/metallic doubling of Garcia's guitar from ~14:00 onward, tape degradation, occasional over‑saturation and general interference make much of the set nearly unlistenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Emotional highs during Dark Star and the closing medley are offset by technical hiccups that cause noticeable dips in momentum, especially after the mid‑set audio failure.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar is obscured by metallic doubling noise; his improvisational flow shines through during Dark Star despite the interference.
band_member_comments.Keys: The organ delivers “nice stuff” that cues Jerry into new realms, adding texture to the standout Dark Star.
